assertion_analysis.text: assert [len(call) for call in writes] == [2, 1] -- independent of the fixture's expectations: writes[0] is the two rows the fake incumbent appends (line 645) and writes[1] is the one row _store_unjudged persists through the monkeypatched write_reviews. Reinstating the pre-incumbent shadow write makes it [1, 2] and fails; logs/base-new-tests.log records exactly that at f69054241.

assert all(row['judge_kind'] == 'incumbent' for row in writes[0]) -- not independent: writes[0] is the fixture's own literal (line 647), so the assertion compares the test's input with itself and holds whatever the code under test does.

assert result['winning_score'] == 0.2 -- weak: 0.2 is the value the fixture's incumbent returns (line 651) and result is the same dict passed through, so the two sides move together; it reddens only if pass-through breaks, not if the cascade's ordering regresses.
assert result is None -- independent of any supplied value: it holds only when the router actually returns the incumbent's None rather than a routed or shadow result.
assert writes == [] -- independent and load-bearing: it reddens precisely when a shadow row is written for a cycle that produced no reviews, which logs/base-new-tests.log confirms at f69054241.

findings.text: follow-on: the gate paragraph states 'nine of them in test_review_release.py', but the arm failure id lists it cites (manifest baseline_suite/after_suite and logs/delta-head.txt) carry twelve head-arm ids in tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py and fourteen across the three test_review_release*.py modules, so the receipt's count does not reconcile with the log it cites; the manifest's own prose says seven for the same set.

follow-on: the same paragraph states the base and head logs 'are recorded with their revision, command and EXIT= line', but logs/head-selection.log opens directly on 'test session starts' and carries no rev=/tree=/cmd= header, unlike logs/base-selection.log, so the head arm's revision cannot be established from the log itself.

follow-on: assert all(row['judge_kind'] == 'incumbent' for row in writes[0]) reads writes[0], which the test's own fake incumbent appended at line 645, so it compares the fixture with itself and cannot fail on any change to cascade.adjudicate_review.

follow-on: assert result['winning_score'] == 0.2 compares the returned dict against the 0.2 the fixture's incumbent supplied at line 651 rather than against an independent source, so it is not a guard on the ordering regression the node exists to fix.
